primitives.does: Identify the unresolved obligation precisely - what was owed that has not been delivered, or what was delivered that is not what was owed. The remedy is chosen to satisfy that rather than to satisfy the complaint, and compensation for the inconvenience is a separate question asked separately

Evaluate the remedies policy actually makes available for this obligation. A remedy that cannot be delivered is not offered - offering one converts a solvable problem into a broken second promise, and the second one costs more than the first

branches.label: No choice to make
branches.test: one remedy applies, or policy determines it

branches.label: Correction or reperformance
